candidates.explanation: The code uses @unchecked Sendable on a class that manages mutable state via an NSLock. While the lock provides synchronization, @unchecked Sendable bypasses the compiler's data race detection, which can lead to issues if the class is accessed in ways the developer did not anticipate.
candidates.title: Use of @unchecked Sendable

candidates.explanation: The 'current' property on the Language enum provides a global mutable state via a singleton. This pattern makes unit testing difficult as it introduces shared state that persists between tests.
candidates.title: Global Mutable State via Singleton

candidates.explanation: The 'make(for:)' method uses a hardcoded default value (.en) when the locale cannot be mapped. This logic is hidden within the method and may lead to unexpected behavior if the mapping fails for reasons other than an unsupported language.
candidates.title: Hardcoded Default Value in Factory Method
